label: row_0
context: This table presents rate constants for the reduction of aldehydes and ketones by sodium borohydride, highlighting how electronic factors govern carbonyl electrophilicity. Aldehydes react much faster than ketones because they possess less electron donation to the carbonyl carbon, leaving it more positively polarized and more susceptible to hydride attack. In ketones, alkyl substituents donate electron density inductively, reducing the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon and slowing reduction. Aromatic conjugation, as in acetophenone and benzophenone, further stabilizes the carbonyl by π delocalization, decreasing its reactivity. Overall, these rates demonstrate that electron-withdrawing environments enhance, and electron-donating environments suppress, nucleophilic addition to carbonyls.
